title: 3D Printing of Personal Protective Equipment and Repurposing of Air Filters
author: Giana Schena
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bd77i9rn

steps.title: Load and scale STL files
steps.instruction: Open the following STL files in your slicer: facemask_filter_guard.stl (currently scaled with the face unit; may need up‑scaling), facemask_face_unit.stl (currently ~female size; may need up‑scaling), facemask_clip.stl, eyemask_thick.stl, eyemask_thin.stl, eyemask_hook.stl, and faceshield_one_unit.stl. For the guard, note that support is not required and its dimensions are 2.5 inches tall, 2.75 inches base length, and 1.6 inches top length. For the face unit and clips, support must be enabled.

steps.title: Set slicer printer parameters
steps.instruction: In your slicer (e.g., Ultimaker Cura) set the following global parameters: Infill density = 30 %; Generate Support = checked; Support Placement = Touching Buildplate; Support Overhang Angle = 45°. For the facemask_clip.stl (and any other clip prints) set the XYZ scaling percentages to 54 %. Keep support enabled for parts that require it (face unit, clips).

steps.title: Print all components
steps.instruction: Print the parts with the settings defined above: facemask_filter_guard.stl (no support), facemask_face_unit.stl (support enabled), two copies of facemask_clip.stl (XYZ = 54 %, support enabled), eyemask_thick.stl, eyemask_thin.stl, eyemask_hook.stl, and faceshield_one_unit.stl. Verify each print finishes before proceeding to the next step.

steps.title: Disinfect printed parts
steps.instruction: Submerge the printed guard and face unit in Clorox bleach for 5 minutes (00:05:00). After soaking, rinse the parts thoroughly with water and allow them to air‑dry completely.

steps.title: Prepare filter material
steps.instruction: Select filter material: for general face‑mask replacement use option 1; for higher protection use option 1 or option 2. Peel the filter off its metal webbing, discard the metal webbing, and keep only the filter material. Cut the filter to fit within the trapezoidal guard dimensions.

steps.title: Assemble mask body
steps.instruction: Place the cut filter between the guard and the face unit, then snap the guard onto the face unit (the fit is very tight but can be released by pressing from inside). Attach an elastic band to the holes on either side of the face unit. If desired, tape or glue padding around the outer edges of the mask for extra comfort.

steps.title: Assemble goggles
steps.instruction: Glue a plexiglass or A4‑size acrylic sheet between the eyemask_thick (outer) and eyemask_thin (inner) prints. Apply foam‑adhesive weather stripping to the inside of the eyemask_thin for comfort. Clip the eyemask_hook print onto the eyemask_thick and secure a 1/2‑inch‑wide elastic band for strapping the goggles to the face. Add any printed facemask_clip pieces as needed and finish with adhesive foam weather stripping and elastic banding to achieve a snug fit.

steps.title: Assemble face shield
steps.instruction: Cut an acrylic sheet to run along the diameter of the faceshield_one_unit opening. The design accommodates A4 sheets and has been tested with 0.10 mm and 0.24 mm thickness sheets. Insert the sheet into the shield; tension in the printed frame holds it in place without screws or clamps.

steps.title: Final fit adjustments
steps.instruction: Add any remaining adhesive foam weather stripping and elastic banding to the mask and goggles to ensure a comfortable, secure fit.
